ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In a certain electrostatic field, the direction of the electric field lines is uncertain, and the distribution is as shown in Figure 8. A charged particle is acted on only by electrostatic force in the electric field, and its trajectory is shown by the dashed line in the figure, moving from M to N. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The acceleration of the particle at point M is less than its acceleration at point N

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a certain electrostatic field, the direction of the electric field lines is uncertain, and the distribution is as shown in Figure 8. A charged particle is acted on only by electrostatic force in the electric field, and its trajectory is shown by the dashed line in the figure, moving from M to N. Compared with the acceleration of the particle at point N, which is greater, the acceleration of the particle at point M or at point N?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The acceleration of the particle at point M is less than its acceleration at point N
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, several curved solid lines can be seen representing electric field lines, and the dashed line represents the trajectory of the charged particle. The particle moves along the dashed line from point M at the lower left to a position near point N at the upper right. The distance between adjacent electric field lines near point M is relatively large, and the electric field lines are relatively sparse; the distance between adjacent electric field lines near point N is relatively small, and the electric field lines are relatively dense. Judging the strength of the electric field according to the density of electric field lines: the denser the electric field lines, the greater the electric field strength. Therefore, the electric field strength at point N is greater than the electric field strength at point M, that is, E_N > E_M. The particle is acted on only by electrostatic force in the electric field; for the same particle, the magnitude of its charge |q| and its mass m do not change, and the magnitude of its acceleration satisfies a = |q|E/m. Therefore a_N > a_M.
